subject: Mental Models
title: The Feynman Technique
description: Learn The Feynman Technique in one minute.

hook.text: Richard Feynman kept a notebook labeled 'Things I Don't Know.' He filled it with explanations written for a child.

buildup.text: His method: pick a concept, explain it simply, find the gaps, then simplify again until a ten-year-old gets it.

discovery.text: If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it. Jargon hides confusion; simplicity reveals it.

twist.text: Experts often resist this test. Their identity is tied to complexity, and simplicity feels threatening.

climax.text: Feynman used this technique on quantum physics. If it worked on quarks, it works on anything.

punchline.text: Explain it to a child. If you can't, learn more.

quiz.question: What is the core test of the Feynman Technique?
options: Explaining the concept in simple language a child could understand
